result.title: FlowBench: Counterfactual Imagination Training for Spatial Intelligence
result.summary: Humans imagine scene changes under hypothetical motions, an ability central to spatial reasoning and robotic planning. However, this capability remains underexplored in vision-language models and world models. We formalize this capability as Counterfactual Spatial Imagination (CSI) and introduce FlowBench, a resource for training and evaluating both, with 428K training examples spanning simulated and real-world scenes, household environments and tabletop manipulation, and diverse question types. A scalable, fully automatic pipeline pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, exact outcome frames and optical flow. For VLMs, proprietary models exhibit an imagination gap, performing worse when motion outcomes must be inferred than when observed, and open-source models perform near chance; fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B on FlowBench-Sim-Train raises its accuracy by 29.5 percentage points in simulation and 16.9 on real images, a strong sim-to-real transfer. For world models, training on FlowBench-Sim improves text-to-flow prediction for all four model families we test, raising the accuracy of Psi-0.6 from 52.1% to 61.7%. FlowBench thus serves as a training and evaluation resource for both. Code and datasets are released at https://github.com/liuyifan22/FlowBench.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「反事实空间想象」（CSI）任务并构建 FlowBench，用 428K 自动生成样本为 VLM 与世界模型提供训练与评测资源，涵盖仿真与真实场景、假设运动后的空间问答及仿真中的真实结果帧与光流。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「想象差距」诊断（模型推断运动结果时明显差于观察时）与微调后 29.5 个百分点的提升，直接涉及 VLM 内部是否保留并使用实体关系与几何信息，可作为检验视觉证据与空间状态表示的评价素材。
